name: Trust Layer and Interaction Standards
purpose: Make every NetCoin workflow feel safe, explainable, and recoverable before additional feature work resumes.
north_star: Every screen answers what is happening, whether it can be trusted, what happens next, and how to recover if something fails.

trust_states.Fresh: Data was recently updated from the expected source.
trust_states.Stale: Data is safe to view but may be out of date.
trust_states.Verified: The result was checked against the expected chain, signature, route, or invariant.
trust_states.Unverified: The result is available but has not yet been independently checked.
trust_states.Risk: The user should review because funds, identity, custody, settlement, or release trust may be affected.

interaction_rules: Every page has exactly one primary action.
Every irreversible action requires a review step before execution.
Every advanced control is hidden behind progressive disclosure until relevant.
Every workflow ends with a reassurance state, a verification link, and one next action.
Every error explains what happened, why it matters, and how to recover.
Every success confirmation is specific to the completed action.
Every trust-critical surface shows freshness, source, and verification status.
Every status color has a text label and must not rely on color alone.
Every copy, export, import, sign, send, withdraw, settle, and verify action gives immediate feedback.
Every new feature must reduce complexity, improve an existing workflow, remove a ceiling, or increase trust/safety/clarity.

microcopy_rules: Prefer plain verbs: Send, Receive, Verify, Review, Export, Retry.
Avoid exposing raw protocol terms before the user asks for advanced details.
Use local-only language for labels, contacts, and notes.
Use exact object names in confirmations: transaction, contact, backup, order, release.
Use reassurance only when it is true and backed by state.
Never imply chain finality before confirmations or active-chain checks exist.
success_criteria: Every trust-critical surface exposes at least three trust signals.
Every irreversible workflow has a review step before execution.
Every workflow defines a success and failure reassurance message.
Every error template includes what happened, why it matters, reassurance, and recovery action.
Every status term is drawn from Healthy, Warning, Offline, Maintenance.
Every UI change can be checked by python tools/check_trust_interaction.py.
